name: Scrape edfringe shows (full)

# Full rebuild: download every show from the edfringe.com GraphQL API, normalize
# into the website-ready data files, and commit them. Run manually from the
# Actions tab. For the lightweight daily top-up see the `refresh-shows` scheduled
# task, which the Claudinite scheduler runs (scraper/README.md).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      per:
        description: Shows per page
        required: false
        default: "50"
      min_delay:
        description: Minimum delay between requests (seconds)
        required: false
        default: "4"
      max_delay:
        description: Maximum delay between requests (seconds)
        required: false
        default: "9"
      commit:
        description: Commit the normalized data back to the repo
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  scrape:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Fetch all shows from the API
        run: |
          python3 scraper/fetch_shows.py \
            --recently-added ANY \
            --per "${{ inputs.per }}" \
            --min-delay "${{ inputs.min_delay }}" \
            --max-delay "${{ inputs.max_delay }}"

      - name: Normalize into website data
        run: python3 scraper/normalize.py

      - name: Summarise
        if: always()
        run: |
          python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('data/days/index.json')); print('shows:',d['shows'],'venues:',d['venues'],'days:',len(d['dates']))" 2>/dev/null || echo "n/a"

      - name: Upload raw scrape artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: edfringe-raw
          path: data/raw_pages/
          retention-days: 90
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Commit normalized data
        if: ${{ inputs.commit }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add data/normalized data/venues.json data/days
          if git diff --staged --quiet; then
            echo "No data changes to commit."
          else
            git commit -m "Update Fringe data (full scrape)"
            git push
          fi

name: Fetch ticket prices (one-off)

# Real ticket amounts for every paid show, into the fetch-once cache
# data/prices.json — then regenerate the site data from it.
#
# Deliberately manual, and deliberately NOT on the nightly path. A show's price
# bands don't change through the festival the way its ticket status does, and
# there is no bulk price endpoint: this is one `performancePrices` call per
# show, ~3,500 of them. Run it once; re-run it only if the festival re-prices.
#
# The pass is resumable — shows already in the cache are skipped — so `limit`
# lets a big run be taken in bites across several runs, each committing what it
# got. See scraper/README.md.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      limit:
        description: Stop after this many newly priced shows (blank = all remaining)
        required: false
        default: ""
      slug:
        description: Price a single show by slug instead (e.g. daniel-sloss-bitter)
        required: false
        default: ""
      min_delay:
        description: Minimum delay between requests (seconds)
        required: false
        default: "1"
      max_delay:
        description: Maximum delay between requests (seconds)
        required: false
        default: "2.5"
      commit:
        description: Commit the price cache and regenerated data back to the repo
        type: boolean
        required: false
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  # Two concurrent runs would both write data/prices.json and race on the push.
  group: fetch-prices
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prices:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 330
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Transform self-test (offline)
        run: python3 scraper/fetch_prices.py --selftest

      - name: Fetch prices
        run: |
          python3 scraper/fetch_prices.py \
            ${{ inputs.slug && format('--slug {0}', inputs.slug) || '--all' }} \
            ${{ inputs.limit && format('--limit {0}', inputs.limit) || '' }} \
            --min-delay "${{ inputs.min_delay }}" \
            --max-delay "${{ inputs.max_delay }}"

      - name: Fold the prices into the site data
        # `always()`, to match the commit step below: when the fetch dies
        # part-way the cache still holds every show it did price, and those
        # belong in the committed site data too. Skipping this on failure would
        # commit a prices.json the day files hadn't caught up with.
        if: always()
        run: python3 scraper/normalize.py --minify-from-master

      - name: Summarise
        if: always()
        run: |
          python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('data/prices.json')); p=list(c['shows'].values()); print('priced shows:', len(p)); print('cheapest:', min(s['min'] for s in p) if p else 'n/a'); print('dearest:', max(s['max'] for s in p) if p else 'n/a')" 2>/dev/null || echo "n/a"

      - name: Commit prices and regenerated data
        # `always()` so an interrupted or partly-failed pass still banks the
        # shows it did price — the cache is resumable and a re-run continues.
        if: ${{ always() && inputs.commit }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add data/prices.json data/normalized data/venues.json data/days
          if git diff --staged --quiet; then
            echo "No price changes to commit."
          else
            git commit -m "Update ticket prices"
            git push
          fi

1	// edfringe task: refresh-tickets — the in-festival, live-ish availability refresh.
2	//
3	// REPLACES the "Refresh today's ticket status (hourly)" workflow, deleted in the
4	// same commit that added this file. That workflow hand-spelled SIXTEEN cron lines to get
5	// "hourly during August, 08:00–23:00 Edinburgh time, on a jittered minute":
6	// `9 7 * 8 *`, `12 8 * 8 *`, `7 9 * 8 *`, … `8 22 * 8 *`. The Claudinite
7	// scheduler is now the repo's only cron, and the migration rule for a cron whose
8	// shape has no frequency token is to declare the frequency and put the
9	// irregularity in the PRECONDITION: the seven cron tokens say *when to evaluate*,
10	// the precondition says *whether to act*. So this is `frequency: 'hourly'` with
11	// an August / 08:00–23:00-Edinburgh gate below. The hand-rolled minute jitter is
12	// dropped outright — the repo's hashed scheduler minute (:49) already staggers
13	// this repo against the rest of the fleet, which is all the jitter was for.
14	//
15	// `agent_model: 'none'` — the whole job is deterministic, so there is no agent
16	// and no dispatch issue: the scheduler runs `agent_preprocessing` as a subprocess
17	// and that is the entire task. A non-zero exit converges the task to one open
18	// `needs-human` issue, replacing the old workflow's `report-failure` job.
19	//
20	// Self-contained (imports nothing). `edinburghClock` and `ticketWindow` are
21	// exported beside the declaration so the window is unit-tested directly
22	// (window.test.mjs) rather than only reasoned about.
23	
24	// August, and the local hours the retired crons covered. The old lines fired at
25	// UTC hours 7…22 inclusive — sixteen firings — which is local 08:xx…23:xx.
26	export const FESTIVAL_MONTH = 8;
27	export const FIRST_LOCAL_HOUR = 8;
28	export const LAST_LOCAL_HOUR = 23;
29	
30	// Europe/London is UTC+1 for the ENTIRE window, so the conversion is a fixed
31	// one-hour shift and needs no timezone database. British Summer Time runs from
32	// the last Sunday in March to the last Sunday in October, so August lies strictly
33	// inside it with months of margin on both sides — there is no DST boundary
34	// anywhere near this window, and any instant whose Edinburgh wall clock reads
35	// August is necessarily under BST. (Instants that shift into any other month are
36	// rejected by the month test regardless, so the offset cannot matter there.)
37	// This is the correction the port had to get right: the scheduler's slot math is
38	// UTC, and reading the UTC hour as if it were local would shift the whole
39	// festival window an hour early.
40	const BST_OFFSET_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000;
41	
42	// The Edinburgh wall-clock month (1–12) and hour (0–23) at UTC instant `now`.
43	export function edinburghClock(now) {
44	  const local = new Date(new Date(now).getTime() + BST_OFFSET_MS);
45	  return { month: local.getUTCMonth() + 1, hour: local.getUTCHours() };
46	}
47	
48	// The precondition's verdict as a pure function of the instant — `{ run, reason }`.
49	export function ticketWindow(now) {
50	  const { month, hour } = edinburghClock(now);
51	  const clock = `${String(hour).padStart(2, '0')}:xx Edinburgh, month ${month}`;
52	  if (month !== FESTIVAL_MONTH) {
53	    return { run: false, reason: `outside the festival — ${clock}; ticket status only moves during August` };
54	  }
55	  // The upper bound is the last hour of the day, so it excludes nothing a
56	  // 0–23 hour could be; it is stated so the window's intent survives an edit.
57	  if (hour < FIRST_LOCAL_HOUR || hour > LAST_LOCAL_HOUR) {
58	    return { run: false, reason: `outside the daily window — ${clock}; the box office moves between ${FIRST_LOCAL_HOUR}:00 and ${LAST_LOCAL_HOUR}:59` };
59	  }
60	  return { run: true, reason: `in-festival and in-window — ${clock}` };
61	}
62	
63	export default {
64	  id: 'refresh-tickets',
65	  frequency: 'hourly',             // evaluate every hour; the precondition decides whether to act
66	  precondition_signals: [],        // the gate is the calendar and the clock, not repo state
67	  agent_model: 'none',             // pure code; the work is the preprocessing subprocess below
68	  expected_outcome: 'none',        // it commits today's ticket statuses straight to the default branch, as the workflow did
69	  agent_instructions: 'worker.sh', // vestigial for an agentless task; the real work is the command below
70	  agent_preprocessing: 'bash worker.sh',
71	  agent_preprocessing_timeout: 900, // the retired workflow's `timeout-minutes: 15`, in seconds
72	
73	  precondition() {
74	    return ticketWindow(new Date());
75	  },
76	};

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# refresh-tickets worker — the ported body of the retired "Refresh today's ticket
# status (hourly)" workflow's job.
#
# The Claudinite scheduler runs this as its `agent_preprocessing` subprocess with
# cwd = this task directory and a hard kill at `agent_preprocessing_timeout`, so
# the first thing it does is move to the repo root the scheduler hands it. There
# is no agent: a non-zero exit is the failure signal, and the scheduler converges
# that to one open `needs-human` issue (the old job's `report-failure` twin).
#
# It only reaches here when task.mjs's precondition says the Edinburgh clock is in
# August, between 08:00 and 23:59 — that gate is the whole of the retired
# workflow's sixteen cron lines. The script itself stays a no-op on any date with
# no day file, so a mis-timed run costs nothing.
#
# Python: the scheduler workflow is a vendored thin shim and cannot carry a
# `setup-python` step, so this uses the runner's own `python3` rather than the
# retired workflow's pinned 3.11. The scraper is standard-library only, so any
# maintained 3.x satisfies it; the guard below fails loudly if there is none.
set -euo pipefail

cd "${CLAUDINITE_REPO_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "refresh-tickets: no python3 on the runner" >&2

input.body:
Corrects #235 (`9246f40`), which diagnosed #231/#141 wrong and shipped a fix that is unsafe in exactly the situation that caused them.

## What #235 got wrong

It claimed `actions/checkout` leaves the branch with no upstream, so the bare `git push` always fails. The scheduler run log disproves both halves:

```
[command]/usr/bin/git checkout --progress --force -B main refs/remotes/origin/main
Switched to a new branch 'main'
branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'.
```

Tracking *is* set, and the bare push has been working: `git log --grep="Refresh today's ticket status"` shows 24 commits, the most recent 2026-08-06 13:25 — i.e. hourly, right through and after the "broken" slot. #231 was one failure, not an hourly one; the 14 comments on it are the watchdog nagging that a stale dispatch issue was never executed, which is a different thing.

## The actual cause

The scheduler runs every due task in **one** checkout. `basics/baselining`'s `deliver()` does `git checkout -B <maintenance branch>` (`.claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs:447`) and never switches back. Any task ordered after a *delivering* baselining runs on a local branch with no upstream — exit 128.

Both failures fit exactly:
- **#231** — run `31016971857`, a manual `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` dispatch. Log: `preprocessing basics/baselining: ok (agent requested)` immediately followed by `! preprocessing edfringe/refresh-tickets: preprocessing exited 128`.
- **#141** — `refresh-shows` on the daily slot baselining shares.

## Why #235's fix is worse than the bug

`git push origin HEAD:main` pushes whatever HEAD is. In the polluted state that *is* the maintenance branch, so the "fix" would push baselining's unreviewed converge commit straight onto `main`, bypassing the maintenance PR that exists to review it. Failing loudly was strictly better than silently publishing.

## This change

Return the checkout to `main` before the scraper writes anything, then push bare:

```bash
current_branch="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
if [ "$current_branch" != "main" ]; then
  echo "…checkout was left on '$current_branch' — returning to main." >&2
  git checkout main
fi
```

`main` is the branch `actions/checkout` created and set tracking on, so the bare push resolves correctly and lands on the intended branch. The task now also *succeeds* on a post-baselining run instead of filing an issue.

Applied to both `refresh-tickets/worker.sh` and `refresh-shows/worker.sh`.

## Not fixed here

The root cause is `deliver()` leaving the working tree on its own branch, in `.claudinite/shared/` — vendored, so a local edit is clobbered by the next vendor refresh. It needs an upstream fix (restore the prior branch, or deliver via plumbing the way `pushGenerated` already does). Filed as #236.

`npm run verify` passes.

input.body:
Root cause behind #231 and #141, found while correcting #235 (see #236).

The scheduler runs every due task in **one** checkout. `basics/baselining`'s `deliver()` does:

```js
git(['-C', root, 'checkout', '-B', branch]);   // .claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs:447
```

and never switches back. Every task ordered after a *delivering* baselining in the same run therefore starts on a local branch with no upstream and with baselining's converge commit at HEAD. For this repo's data workers that surfaced as `preprocessing exited 128` on the bare `git push`:

- #231 — run `31016971857`, a manual `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` dispatch: `baselining: ok (agent requested)` then `refresh-tickets: preprocessing exited 128`.
- #141 — `refresh-shows`, on the daily slot baselining shares.

The blast radius is wider than a failed push: any later task that commits is committing onto baselining's branch, and any that pushes by explicit refspec would publish baselining's unreviewed converge past its own maintenance PR.

Two candidate fixes upstream, both local to `deliver()`:
- restore the previous branch after the push (record `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` first, `git checkout -` at the end, including on the failure path); or
- build and push the maintenance commit with plumbing and never touch the working tree — `pushGenerated()` in `deliver-generated.mjs` already does exactly this.

The second matches the engine's own precedent and has no restore-on-failure path to get wrong.

`.claudinite/shared/` is vendored here, so this can't be fixed in this repo — a local edit is clobbered by the next vendor refresh. #236 works around it by returning the checkout to `main` at the top of each edfringe worker.

Now your actual question — plus the correction I hit while answering it.

## scrape.yml and prices.yml

Both are **manual, human-triggered full rebuilds** — `workflow_dispatch` only, no `schedule`.

- **`scrape.yml`** ("Scrape edfringe shows (full)") downloads *every* show from the edfringe GraphQL API, normalizes, commits. 60-minute timeout, uploads the raw pages as a 90-day artifact. Inputs: page size, request delays, and `commit`.
- **`prices.yml`** ("Fetch ticket prices (one-off)") calls `performancePrices` once per show — ~3,500 calls, 330-minute timeout — into the fetch-once cache `data/prices.json`, then regenerates site data. Resumable: cached shows are skipped, so `limit` lets a big run be taken in bites. Its header says why it's deliberately off the nightly path: price bands don't move during the festival the way availability does, and there's no bulk endpoint.

## Why they aren't Claudinite tasks

Different axis for each:

**Trigger.** The Claudinite scheduler is the repo's *only* cron (`claudinite-scheduler.yml`, hourly on hashed minute :49). These two have no cron at all — a human decides when a 60-minute or 5.5-hour scrape is worth running. Nothing to migrate.

**Shape.** A task isn't a workflow; it's a declaration plus a worker the scheduler runs as a subprocess in its own checkout. `refresh-tickets/task.mjs` declares `frequency: 'hourly'` and puts the irregularity in a `precondition()` — that's the whole of the retired workflow's *sixteen* hand-spelled cron lines ("August, 08:00–23:59 Edinburgh"). `agent_model: 'none'` means the worker is the entire task, and a non-zero exit converges to one open `needs-human` issue, replacing the old `report-failure` job.

**What each shape can carry.** The workflows own their runner: `setup-python@v5` pinned to 3.11, artifacts, `concurrency`, `permissions`, dispatch inputs. The tasks get none of that — the scheduler workflow is a vendored thin shim, so `worker.sh` uses the runner's own `python3` and has no inputs, which is why the one-off escape hatches are documented as manual commands in the comments.

**Load-bearing consequence:** every due task shares *one* checkout, whereas each workflow gets a fresh one. That's the whole bug below.

## The correction

While tracing whether `scrape.yml`/`prices.yml` had the same push bug, I checked the run logs and found my #235 diagnosis was wrong — and the fix actively unsafe.

- `actions/checkout` **does** set tracking: `branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'`. The bare `git push` was fine — 24 ticket-refresh commits landed hourly, including after the "broken" slot. #231 was **one** failure; its 14 comments are the watchdog nagging about a stale unexecuted dispatch issue, which is a different failure entirely. "Failing every hour since 08-05" wasn't right, and I repeated it instead of checking.
- Real cause: `basics/baselining`'s `deliver()` runs `git checkout -B <maintenance branch>` and never switches back. Later tasks in the same run inherit a branch with no upstream. #231 was a manual `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` run — the log shows baselining "ok" then `refresh-tickets: exited 128` two minutes later. #141 is `refresh-shows` on baselining's daily slot.
- **`git push origin HEAD:main` was the dangerous part**: from that polluted checkout it pushes baselining's *unreviewed converge commit* onto main, past its own maintenance PR. Failing loudly was better.

[PR #236](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/236) reverts that and returns the checkout to `main` before the scraper runs; [#237](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/237) tracks the upstream `deliver()` fix (vendored, so unfixable here). I corrected the record on #231 and #141.

So: `scrape.yml` and `prices.yml` never had this bug. Their bare `git push` is correct, and they can't hit checkout pollution — they run alone.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#236](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/236) needs review (it corrects a bad change already on main), and [#237](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/237) needs the upstream Claudinite fix.

upstream, so the bare `git push` in the refresh-tickets worker aborted with
exit 128 ("The current branch has no upstream branch"). Every hourly run

pages.yml. refresh-shows carried the identical bug (#141) and is fixed the

**1. `main` is carrying a hazard right now — mine.** `9246f40` (#235, which you merged on my wrong diagnosis) makes both data workers push `origin HEAD:main`. It's conditional — it only fires when baselining *delivers* before a data task in the same scheduler run — but it is live. Before my change that case failed loudly; now it publishes silently. [#236](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/236) reverts it and is the thing waiting on CI.

**2. The actual underlying bug is unfixed — [#237](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/237).** `basics/baselining`'s `deliver()` does `git checkout -B <maintenance branch>` and never switches back, so every task ordered after it in the same run inherits a polluted checkout. That's what broke #231 and #141. It lives in `.claudinite/shared/` (vendored), so it can't be fixed here — #236 only works around it per-worker.

**3. CI is failing for GitHub's reasons, not ours.** Two attempts on #236:
- First: sat `queued` 15 minutes, cancelled without ever starting, no logs.
- Second: started, then died in `Prepare all required actions` — `Failed to resolve action download info. Error: Service Unavailable`, twice retried, then error.

That's GitHub Actions service degradation before a single step of ours ran. `npm run verify` passes locally, and the same workflow went green on this branch's previous head. I've queued a third re-run.

if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then

# Return the checkout to `main` before touching anything. The scheduler runs
# EVERY due task in ONE checkout, and `basics/baselining`'s deliver() does
# `git checkout -B <maintenance branch>` and never switches back — so a task

# Not `git push origin HEAD:main`: from a polluted checkout that would push
# baselining's unreviewed converge straight to main, past its maintenance PR.
current_branch="$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"
if [ "$current_branch" != "main" ]; then
  echo "refresh-tickets: checkout was left on '$current_branch' — returning to main." >&2
